setting.title: The Kestrel Hill Meteorite
setting.premise: Odette Vane, a retired astronomer, has invited four members of her stargazing club to her hilltop farmhouse for the meteor shower weekend and her 75th birthday on Sunday. On Friday night the meteorite she found on this hill in 1986 vanished from its glass box in her backyard dome.
setting.missingItem: a walnut-sized iron meteorite in a glass-lidded box

guests.name: Roz Thackery
guests.role: a science teacher who joined the club in March
guests.voice: 44. Brisk and capable. Full sentences, capitals and full stops, all short. Says 'Right.' and 'Honestly.' Uses 👍 now and then and no other emoji.

away.status: at the village shop for birthday candles

wrongProof: That's got nothing to do with what I said.
I'm not sure what you think that proves.

questions.ask: Where were you after the session on Friday?

lines.text: Came in with everyone about half eleven.
Bed by half past. Out like a light.

pressed.text: Out like a light. Long week of marking.

questions.ask: When did you last see the meteorite?

lines.text: Quarter past eleven. Odette passed it round in the dome, then put it back on the shelf.

pressed.text: Quarter past eleven. We all saw it.

questions.ask: Did you see or hear anything on Friday night?

lines.text: Nothing. I sleep like the dead.

questions.ask: Who do you think took it?

lines.text: Desmond was creaking about on the stairs at some point. Draw your own conclusions.

lines.text: Bright girl. Cagey about uni, if you ask me.

questions.ask: What do you make of Desmond?

lines.text: Guards the club accounts like they're the crown jewels. Harmless, probably.

questions.ask: What do you make of Wren?

lines.text: Talks a lot. Takes a nice photo. 👍

questions.ask: How do you know Odette?

lines.text: Through the club. I joined in March.

questions.ask: Have you been to Kestrel Hill before?

lines.text: Never. First time up here. Lovely spot.

caught.text: Fine. Once. I was six.
Dad brought me to a star party. It was a long time ago.

questions.ask: Why did your dad bring you to Kestrel Hill?

lines.text: He and Odette found that meteorite together. Top field, August 1986.
She kept it. He never minded. I did, a bit.

questions.ask: Were you out with your headlamp after midnight on Friday?

lines.text: No. I lent it to Pip after the session. She couldn't find hers.

caught.text: Right. Fine. I had it.
I went out about quarter to one for a last look at the meteors.
Stayed on the lawn. Nowhere near the dome.

questions.ask: Did you go into the dome when you were out at quarter to one?

lines.text: No. Lawn, sky, meteors. Twenty minutes.

caught.text: Fine. I went in. I wanted to see it once more, on my own.
I didn't take it.

questions.ask: Is that AA battery by the dome door yours?

lines.text: Not mine. My headlamp takes those flat coin cells.

caught.text: Alright, it takes AAs. Batteries fall out of things.
Doesn't make me a thief.

questions.ask: What did you do in the dome during the session?

lines.text: Counted meteors. Forty-one by eleven. Odette was thrilled.

questions.ask: Where are you sleeping?

lines.text: Back bedroom, end of the landing.

questions.ask: How was dinner on Friday?

lines.text: Good. Odette's stew, then everyone out to the dome by nine.

questions.ask: Anything odd this morning?

lines.text: Odette in tears in the dome. That's odd enough.

questions.ask: Where were you on Saturday night?

lines.text: Bed by eleven. Didn't stir.

questions.ask: Anything odd this morning?

lines.text: Frost's all scuffed round the dome door. Half the club playing detective, I expect.

questions.ask: Where were you on Sunday night?

lines.text: Bed by eleven. Early start today.

lines.text: No. Slept straight through.

questions.ask: What do you make of the box turning up under Wren's bag?

pressed.text: I'm only saying what it looks like.

lines.text: Apart from the box in the barn? No.

questions.ask: When are you heading home?

guests.name: Desmond Hale
guests.role: the club's treasurer and keeper of its logbooks
guests.voice: 61, a retired accountant. Courteous and exact: full sentences, proper punctuation, times to the minute. No emoji. Says 'I must say' when flustered.

away.status: driving to the village for milk

questions.ask: Where were you after the session on Friday?

lines.text: In my room from 11:30. I didn't set foot outside all night.

pressed.text: I was in my room. I'm quite certain.

caught.text: Oh dear. Yes. I went back to the dome at 1:38.
I'd knocked the finder scope out of line during the session and couldn't bear for Odette to find it. I put it right.
That is all I did, I promise you.

questions.ask: Was the meteorite there when you went into the dome at 1:38?

lines.text: No. I noticed the glass box was empty at about 1:40.
I assumed Odette had taken it in for the night. I wish I'd said.

pressed.text: Empty. I am sure of it.

questions.ask: Why didn't you just tell Odette about the finder scope?

lines.text: Pride, I suppose. It was her late husband's telescope.

questions.ask: When did you last see the meteorite?

lines.text: At 11:15. Odette passed it round and put it back on the dome shelf.

questions.ask: Did you see or hear anything on Friday night?

lines.text: The back stairs creaked at some point after midnight. I didn't look at the clock.

questions.ask: Who do you think took it?

lines.text: I'd rather not guess. Though I gather Pip was up and about late.

pressed.text: It was only a light under her door.

questions.ask: What do you make of Roz?

lines.text: Very capable. Keeps her own counsel.

pressed.text: I hardly know her. She only joined in March.

questions.ask: What do you make of Pip?

lines.text: A lovely girl. I gather her studies aren't going brilliantly, but that's hardly my business.

questions.ask: What do you make of Wren?

pressed.text: The March issue. I keep them all.

questions.ask: Whose headlamp flickers?

lines.text: Roz's. She was thumping it all through Friday's session.
Loose battery, I'd say.

pressed.text: Roz's. I sat next to her.

questions.ask: Has anyone borrowed batteries from you this weekend?

lines.text: Yes, Roz. I gave her two AAs at dinner on Friday, for her headlamp.

pressed.text: Two AAs. I keep a pack in the car.

questions.ask: Has Roz really never been to Kestrel Hill before?

lines.text: Funny you should ask. I went through the club's old logbooks last winter.
The 1986 star party here lists 'R. Thackery, aged 6'.

pressed.text: It's in the logbook. I can show you.

questions.ask: Where did the meteorite come from?

lines.text: Odette found it in the top field in August 1986, with a club friend. She has never said which one.

pressed.text: Before my time in the club, sadly.

questions.ask: What do you do for the club?

lines.text: Treasurer, for my sins. And keeper of the logbooks, back to 1979.

questions.ask: How do you know Odette?

lines.text: We've been in the club together for thirty years. She's the reason I took up astronomy.

questions.ask: What happened during the session?

lines.text: Forty-one meteors by eleven. Odette brought out the meteorite to celebrate.

pressed.text: A very good night, until it wasn't.

questions.ask: Anything odd this morning?

lines.text: Only Odette. I've never seen her so upset.

questions.ask: Where are you sleeping?

lines.text: The little room at the top of the stairs. It creaks dreadfully.

questions.ask: Where were you on Saturday night?

lines.text: Awake at two, I'm afraid. I made cocoa in the kitchen.

pressed.text: Cocoa, at two. Then back to bed.

questions.ask: Did you see anything odd on Saturday night?

questions.ask: If you had to name someone today, who would it be?

lines.text: I'd hate to. But the box was under Wren's bag.

questions.ask: When are you heading home?

lines.text: Once I've loaded the car. This afternoon.

timeline.text: Odette passes the meteorite round in the dome and puts it back on the shelf. Everyone heads in by 11:30.
Wren sets up a timelapse in the barn.
Pip creeps down to the kitchen and eats a slice of Odette's birthday cake.
Roz slips out the back door with her flickering headlamp, leaving her phone charging upstairs.
Roz takes the meteorite from the dome. Her headlamp's loose AA battery drops in the frost by the door. She's back out at 12:57, caught on Wren's timelapse.
Desmond sneaks into the dome to fix the finder scope he knocked, and notices the empty box without thinking much of it.
Roz goes out and pockets the battery by the dome door.
Desmond can't sleep and makes cocoa.
Wren leaves her camera bag in the barn.
With her headlamp dead, Roz uses her phone as a torch to slip the empty glass box under Wren's camera bag in the barn. The meteorite is in her car, meant for her late father's memorial.
